statement: Two pre-existing count-parity completeness tests gate `RulePack` registry rows in this workspace: `enforcer-lang-security/tests/completeness.rs` pins the `SEC-*` family registry (`rules::registry::build_all`) to exactly 22 rows against `rules/rules.json`'s `family=="security"` count, and `enforcer-scan`/`enforcer-scan tests/router.rs` assert exact `plan.rule_packs` vectors for specific fixtures. Adding new rule rows into an EXISTING completeness-gated registry (rather than a fresh sibling registry) or adding a new always-on `RulePack` variant WILL break these exact-equality assertions even though nothing is logically wrong.
why: h11 needed to register 11 CYBER-* rules in enforcer-lang-security and one new cross-cutting RulePack::SecurityAudit in enforcer-scan's router; naively adding rows to the existing SEC-* build_all() would have desynced the 22-count oracle against rules/rules.json, and adding SecurityAudit to build_route_plan's always-on set broke two exact vec![...] assertions in plan.rs and router.rs that predated this pack.
howToApply: Before adding rows to any registry or a new always-on classification variant, grep for `assert_eq!` against that registry's `.len()` or an exact `Vec`/`vec![...]` equality on the enum in question. If a completeness oracle pins an existing family to a fixed count, mint a SEPARATE registry function (own module, own build_all) rather than growing the pinned one. If adding a new always-on enum variant, update every exact-vec assertion that will now include it (searched: `rule_packs,\n` and `rule_packs ==`).

statement: `enforcer-scan/src/walk.rs`'s `glob_matches` only strips a SINGLE trailing/leading `*` (`glob.strip_suffix('*')`), so a double-star pattern like `vendor/**` degrades to a literal prefix check against `"vendor/*"` (with the literal asterisk character) and NEVER matches real paths -- it silently fails closed to 'nothing ignored', not 'everything under vendor ignored'. This bug already existed in the shipped `ocentra-enforcer.json` profile's `tests/fixtures/enforcer/**` and `profiles/*/legacy-scripts/**` entries before h11 touched the file.
why: h11's dogfood-exclusion acceptance criterion required `vendor/**` (or equivalent) in `ignoreFileGlobs` to actually exclude `vendor/anthropic-cybersecurity-skills/**` from a real walk of the repo; using `**` per the workpack's own prose would have silently passed catalog-shape validation while doing nothing at scan time.
howToApply: In this repo's TODAY's glob matcher, use a SINGLE trailing star (`vendor/*`) for a prefix-style directory exclusion -- `glob.strip_suffix('*')` turns that into `starts_with("vendor/")`, which correctly matches every nested path. Do not add new `**`-suffixed ignoreFileGlobs entries expecting recursive-glob semantics until `glob_matches` itself is fixed to handle `**` (flagged as a separate, out-of-scope defect - the existing `tests/fixtures/enforcer/**` and `profiles/*/legacy-scripts/**` entries are likely ALSO silently inert and worth auditing).

statement: The vendored `anthropic-cybersecurity-skills` corpus (817 skills, Apache-2.0) IS present at `vendor/anthropic-cybersecurity-skills/` in this worktree at h11 build time. Its 817 SKILL.md frontmatter blocks were unioned by a hand-rolled Rust line-scanner (no serde_yaml dependency added -- the frontmatter shape is a flat `key: scalar` / `key:\n- item` list, never nested mappings) into a non-trivial `mitre_attack`/`nist_csf` id set, confirmed live by `enforcer-security::cyberskills::vocab::tests::corpus_union_seeds_a_non_trivial_dictionary_when_vendor_present` scanning the real vendor directory (not a fixture stand-in) at test time.
why: The workpack's L12 vendor-absent protocol required recording corpus presence/absence honestly rather than assuming either; this pack found it PRESENT, so the h03 vocab seed and dogfood-exclusion tests both exercise the real vendor tree (skipping gracefully to Ok(()) only if the dir is later removed), which is stronger proof than a synthetic fixture would have given.
howToApply: Any future pack that also depends on `vendor/anthropic-cybersecurity-skills/` should follow the same pattern: gate real-corpus tests with an `if !vendor_dir.is_dir() { return Ok(()); }` early-return (never fabricate corpus content, never hard-fail if a CI/consumer checkout lacks the vendor tree via .gitignore/submodule-not-fetched), and keep at least one assertion that would fail if the vendor tree silently went empty (skills_scanned > 0).
